name: OWASP Top 10 2025
description: The OWASP Top 10 2025 — ten standalone vulnerable corporate applications.

labs.title: A01:2025
labs.name: Broken Access Control
labs.description: Restrictions on what authenticated users are allowed to do are often not properly enforced.

labs.title: A02:2025
labs.name: Security Misconfiguration
labs.description: The most commonly seen issue. Without a concerted, repeatable hardening process, systems are at risk.

labs.title: A03:2025
labs.name: Software Supply Chain Failures
labs.description: Software and data integrity failures relate to code and infrastructure that does not protect against integrity violations.

labs.title: A04:2025
labs.name: Cryptographic Failures
labs.description: Failures related to cryptography which often lead to exposure of sensitive data or system compromise.

labs.title: A05:2025
labs.name: Injection
labs.description: User-supplied data is not validated, filtered, or sanitised by the application.

labs.title: A06:2025
labs.name: Insecure Design
labs.description: A broad category representing different weaknesses, expressed as missing or ineffective control design.

labs.title: A07:2025
labs.name: Authentication Failures
labs.description: Confirmation of the user's identity, authentication, and session management is critical.

labs.title: A08:2025
labs.name: Software or Data Integrity Failures
labs.description: Code and infrastructure that does not protect against integrity violations.

labs.title: A09:2025
labs.name: Security Logging & Alerting Failures
labs.description: Without logging and monitoring, breaches cannot be detected.

labs.title: A10:2025
labs.name: Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions
labs.description: Applications that fail to handle error conditions safely can expose internal state.

a01.text: User identifiers in the URLs are sequential integers. There are at least 4 registered users in the system.
Try modifying the numeric ID in /profile/N with different values. Does the server verify that the requested profile belongs to you?
The document reader builds the file path by concatenating user input without sanitisation. Try sequences like ../ to escape the base directory and read server files.

a02.text: Misconfigured servers often have diagnostic endpoints active in production and configuration files publicly accessible.
Try common paths: /debug, /config, /backup. Default credentials are a common risk in administration panels.
There is a /backup directory with file listing enabled. The .sql and .csv files inside contain credentials and internal tokens.

a03.text: The listed dependency versions date from 2018-2020. Cross-reference them against public CVE databases to identify critical vulnerabilities.
Search NVD or OSV for the installed versions. One of the packages has a CRITICAL-rated CVE for arbitrary code execution.
pyyaml 3.13 is affected by CVE-2020-1747 (CRITICAL). The install simulator accepts internal package names that could be hijacked on public PyPI.

a04.text: The system stores credentials using a hashing algorithm designed for speed, not security. The hashes are visible in the application.
MD5 without salt is crackable in seconds with rainbow tables. Tools like CrackStation or hashcat -m 0 can reverse it instantly.
JWT tokens use a short, predictable secret. Decode the JWT, change the payload to role=admin, and re-sign it with the correct secret using jwt.io.

a05.text: The store search form builds database queries by directly concatenating user input without parameterisation.
Try classic SQL injection: a single quote breaks the query. UNION SELECT lets you retrieve data from other tables, including a secrets table.
The connectivity tool passes user input directly to a system command. Append ; followed by OS commands to execute code on the server.

a06.text: The shopping system does not validate the range of numeric values submitted in the order form.
Submitting a negative quantity produces a negative total. The system processes it without any restrictions.
There is an administration panel accessible without real authentication. The URL does not appear in the visible navigation but the endpoint is active.

a07.text: The login system does not implement any mechanism to protect against repeated failed authentication attempts.
Thousands of login attempts can be made without lockout or CAPTCHA. Account passwords are short and common.
The password reset token is generated predictably using the user's email and a rounded timestamp. It is reproducible if you know both values.

a08.text: The update system accepts serialised data from the client and processes it without verifying its integrity or origin.
Python pickle executes arbitrary code during deserialisation. Define a class with __reduce__ returning a tuple (os.system, ('command',)) and serialise it in base64.
Session cookies are Python dicts encoded in base64 without an HMAC signature. Modify the role field to admin, re-encode in base64 and replace the cookie.

a09.text: The system logs authentication events including more information than strictly necessary.
The system log file is publicly accessible. Successful login entries include the user's credentials in plain text.
The report form writes user input directly to the log file without any sanitisation, allowing injection of fake log entries.

a10.text: The application does not properly handle runtime errors and exposes internal server information in HTTP responses.
Sending unexpected data types or JSON structures with missing keys triggers unhandled exceptions that include the full stack trace with configuration variables.
Certain endpoints have a try/except block that catches TypeError but returns sensitive data as part of the error handler. Try non-existent resource IDs.

a06_obscur.name: Hidden admin panel — security by obscurity
